concerns.text: FR-012 requires retrieving reference functional group frequencies from the NIST Chemistry WebBook to validate attention peaks. The plan.md 'Technical Context' and 'Constitution Check' sections mention using NIST for 'validation of attention peaks' but do not specify the mechanism for retrieving these reference values (e.g., static lookup table, API call, or local file). Without a defined retrieval method in the plan, the implementer cannot satisfy the requirement to 'retrieve' data, risking a failure to measure SC-003.

FR-009 mandates a sensitivity analysis over a set of three thresholds: {[deferred], [deferred], [deferred]}. The plan.md 'Methodology' section (3.4 Evaluation) mentions generating heatmaps but does not explicitly state that a sensitivity analysis over three distinct thresholds will be performed. The plan must include a specific step or task to execute this sensitivity analysis to ensure SC-003b (robustness) is measured.

FR-015 requires a 'Simulated Data Integrity Check' to verify simulated spectra are not deterministic functions of fingerprints. The plan.md 'Research' section (2.2 Data Integration) discusses a 'Simulated Data Path' but does not explicitly describe the implementation of the integrity check (e.g., computing collinearity or VIF on the generated synthetic data) as a distinct step before training. The plan must ensure this check is a defined phase to satisfy the requirement.

FR-016 requires computing the Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) between spectral and fingerprint inputs. While the plan.md 'Research' section (2.2) mentions computing VIF, it is listed under 'Data Integrity Checks' for simulated data. The requirement applies to the general system (See Scientific Soundness). The plan must explicitly include VIF computation as a standard evaluation step for the final model, not just a conditional check for simulated data pivots, to ensure SC-003 is fully measured.
